title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§6 of the notes, 'Relations avec stratifications de type I'). I is a finite poset. A stratification of type I of X is an increasing family of closed subspaces (X_i), i in I. It is called 'privilégiée' when three conditions hold:
- (a) for j' an immediate predecessor of j, X_{j'} sits in X_j as a 'bordant' subspace, i.e. a collared boundary piece.
- (b) transversality conditions on the boundary pieces and their cylinders.
- (c) for i <= j, let S be the set of immediate predecessors of j in the interval I_{ij}. The map k -> s_k = {s in S : k <= s} is an anti-isomorphism I_{ij} -> P(S). So every closed interval is a Boolean lattice.

The header of this page states the geometric meaning of (c). Near X_i, the space X_j with its induced stratification by the interval I_{ij} is modelled on the corner of an n-cube, n = card S. This is the 'cubique' case. The sketch shows a 2-dimensional corner (a square angle) with a hatched wedge, i.e. a lower stratum emanating from the corner.

Combinatorial lemma. Suppose:
- J' is an immediate predecessor of J;
- K <= J but K is not <= J';
- some i satisfies i <= K and i <= J'.
Then K' = inf(K, J') exists and K' is an immediate predecessor of K.

Proof. Pass to the interval [i, J], which is Boolean, ~ P(F); P(F) is self-dual, so iso vs anti-iso is irrelevant. There:
- inf is intersection;
- J = J' ⊔ {α};
- K ⊂ J with K not ⊂ J' forces α ∈ K, so K = K' ⊔ {α} with K' = K ∩ J'.

Geometric step. Consider the commutative square
X_{K'} -> X_K
  |          |
X_{J'} -> X_J
The arrow X_{J'} -> X_J is bordant by hypothesis (6a). Grothendieck labels the vertical arrows (K <= J, K' <= J') bordant too, by (6); strictly, (6a) covers only immediate-predecessor inclusions. He then begins to conclude, 'by b, c', that the pair (X_K, X_{K'}) -> (X_J, X_{J'}) is a morphism of 'bordered pairs'. Presumably this means two things:
- X_K ∩ X_{J'} = X_{K'};
- the collar of X_{J'} in X_J restricts to a collar of X_{K'} in X_K.
This is the compatibility of faces needed to build the stratified space locally as a manifold-with-corners-like object. That is the 'déploiement' (unfolding) programme of the folder, to be connected in §7 with systems of transversal cylinders and conical neighbourhoods. The sentence breaks off at the page end.
errors: The lemma's inf is proved inside the interval [i,J] only. The inf of K and J' in all of I would also require every lower bound not >= i to lie below K'. Grothendieck's 'la inf existe' is only justified locally, i.e. in [i,J] or for elements above i. The 'immediate predecessor' claim is fine, since intervals are convex.
'K ∈ J' in the parenthetical proof should be 'K ⊂ J' (a notational slip in the P(F) model).

Previous page states (c) as an anti-isomorphism with P(S), while this page argues with an isomorphism to P(F) (predecessor = remove one element). Harmless, because P(F) is self-dual via complement, but inconsistent notation.

The verticals X_{K'}→X_{J'} and X_K→X_J are called bordant 'par l'hyp. (6)'. (6a) only covers immediate predecessors; for general K <= J, a bordant/corner inclusion requires iterating, which is itself what is being established. This is a minor circularity or gap. The final conclusion is unfinished.

ideas.what: Stratification indexed by a finite poset where every interval [i,j] is a Boolean lattice, giving a local model of X_j along X_i as the corner of an n-cube, n = number of immediate predecessors
ideas.modern_name: manifolds with corners / ⟨n⟩-manifolds (face posets locally Boolean); cubical stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jänich (1968, ⟨n⟩-manifolds), Douady (1961, variétés à bord anguleux), Laures (2000)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 discusses déploiement of tame stratified spaces only in general terms

ideas.what: Lemma: in a poset with Boolean intervals, for J' a predecessor of J and K <= J, K not <= J' with a common lower bound, inf(K,J') exists locally and is a predecessor of K
ideas.modern_name: elementary Boolean lattice combinatorics (face of a face in a cube)

ideas.what: Compatibility of collars: a square of bordant inclusions (X_K, X_{K'}) -> (X_J, X_{J'}) giving face-compatibility in the 'unfolded' stratified space
ideas.modern_name: compatible collars on manifolds with corners; resolution/unfolding of Thom–Mather stratified spaces into manifolds with corners
ideas.where_published: déploiement mentioned in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and Récoltes et Semailles, no details

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic, poset-indexed framework of 'privileged' stratifications. Conditions are bordant inclusions for successors, transversal cylinders, and Boolean intervals. The aim is to show such stratified spaces are locally corners of cubes and to pass to conical neighbourhoods. The page breaks off mid-argument. This is an independent, combinatorially explicit approach to unfolding stratified spaces into manifold-with-corners-like objects, predating similar resolutions in the literature.
missed.quote: Structure locale de X_J le long d'un X_i (avec la stratification induite ... I_{ij}), cas "cubique" (coin de cube de dimension n=card S)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects to the Ayala–Francis–Tanaka unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces and to ALMP resolutions. A poset-axiomatic version (Boolean intervals plus collars) is close to, but not identical with, ⟨n⟩-manifold formalisms. It is of historical interest; probably not new mathematically to specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine combinatorial lemma plus a set-up step in Grothendieck's unpublished déploiement programme. The cubical/Boolean-interval local model is essentially the manifold-with-corners picture already known (Douady, Jänich). Historically it documents the details behind the Esquisse's déploiement idea, but contains no unexpected result.
transcription_corrections: The first-line word read as 'drapeaux' is uncertain from the image.
'K ∈ J mais non K ⊂ J'' — the image indeed shows ∈, but ⊂ is meant.
The left marginal note (transcribed 'σ avec pr.') is largely illegible; it may read 'c'est pour' or similar, so the reading is uncertain.
The left diagram shows J' ↔(préd) J on top, double arrows ⇓ to K' ↔ K, and i with arrows to J' and K. That is, i is a common minorant, consistent with the text.
The final line reads 'on voit (par b, c) que (X_K, X_{K'}) → (X_J, X_{J'})', with the crossed-out '(X_K → X' before it.
